photo.fileTitle: File:A selection of instruments used for monitoring volcanoes.jpg
photo.caption: A multi-component gas analyzer system is often one of many instruments used to measure gases and monitor volcanic activity.
photo.description: This image depicts instruments used in volcano monitoring. These were deployed in the vicinity of Mount Merapi in 2014.

photo.caption: Multi-GAS permanent field station. Set-up consists of a Multi-GAS, satellite terminal, 12V batteries, and solar panel control located inside the wooden box. Satellite antenna, solar panels, and multi-GAS intake/outtake located outside of the box.
photo.description: Multi-GAS station used to measure volcanic gases. Measures CO2, SO2, H2S. Helps understand volcano activity.

rights.fileTitle: File:Example of CO2 H2S multi-GAS data.png

photo.fileTitle: File:Example of CO2 H2S multi-GAS data.png
photo.caption: Raw multi-GAS data showing the correlation between CO2 and H2S. Fitting a linear regression line to raw data allows for the calculation of the CO2/H2S ratio for monitoring changes in the gas output of the system.
photo.description: This is an example of what raw data from a Multi-GAS may look like. The axes include volcanic gases CO2 and H2S. The slope represents the linear regression and R is the correlation coefficient.
